english: Let $a$, $b$ and $c$ be real numbers such that the system of equations
has no solution and no two of the planes $P_1:\ x-2y+2z=3$, $P_2:\ 2x+ay+bz=1$, $P_3:\ 3x-6y+cz=-12$ have a common point. The line
meets the plane, among $P_1$, $P_2$, $P_3$, that is farthest from the origin at the point $Q$. Then the $z$-coordinate of $Q$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $a$, $b$ तथा $c$ ऐसी वास्तविक संख्याएँ हैं कि समीकरण निकाय
का कोई हल नहीं है तथा तलों $P_1:\ x-2y+2z=3$, $P_2:\ 2x+ay+bz=1$, $P_3:\ 3x-6y+cz=-12$ में से किन्हीं दो का कोई उभयनिष्ठ बिन्दु नहीं है। रेखा
तलों $P_1$, $P_2$, $P_3$ में से मूलबिन्दु से सबसे दूर स्थित तल को बिन्दु $Q$ पर मिलती है। तब $Q$ का $z$-निर्देशांक ______ है।
solution: Pairwise disjoint planes are parallel: normals $\propto(1,-2,2)$, so $a=-4$, $b=4$, $c=6$
Planes $x-2y+2z=c_i$ with $c_1=3$, $c_2=\frac12$, $c_3=-4$; distances from $O$: $\frac{|c_i|}{3}=1,\ \frac16,\ \frac43$, so $P_3$ is farthest
Point of $L$: $(1+2t,\ -1+t,\ -t)$; $x-2y+2z=3-2t$ (direction $\cdot$ normal $=-2\ne0$, so $L$ meets each plane)
solution_full: Two planes without a common point are parallel and distinct, so the normals $(2,a,b)$ and $(3,-6,c)$ are multiples of $(1,-2,2)$: $a=-4$, $b=4$ (factor $2$) and $c=6$ (factor $3$).
Dividing by these factors: $P_1:\ x-2y+2z=3$, $P_2:\ x-2y+2z=\frac12$, $P_3:\ x-2y+2z=-4$. The constants are distinct, so the planes are pairwise disjoint and the system has no solution, as required.
The distance of the origin from $x-2y+2z=c$ is $\dfrac{|c|}{\sqrt{1+4+4}}=\dfrac{|c|}{3}$: $1$ for $P_1$, $\frac16$ for $P_2$, $\frac43$ for $P_3$. So $P_3$ is the farthest.
A general point of $L$ is $(1+2t,\ -1+t,\ -t)$. The direction $(2,1,-1)$ has dot product $2-2-2=-2\ne0$ with the normal, so $L$ is not parallel to the planes and meets each in exactly one point.
originality_note: New: an inconsistent system whose three planes are forced to be parallel and disjoint, then ranked by distance from the origin, and finally cut by a line (way 5). Closest known: conditions for parallel planes, and the point where a line meets a plane. Different because: the plane to be used is chosen by a distance comparison after the parallel conditions, linking the system to line-plane geometry.
blueprint_concepts: Solving system of linear equations when all three planes are parallel and disjoint

concept_use.Solving system of linear equations when: No solution with no two planes meeting forces the three planes to be parallel and distinct, giving a = -4, b = 4, c = 6.
concept_use.Line and a plane: The line L is written parametrically and meets the plane P3 where 3 - 2t = -4; its direction is not perpendicular to the normal, so the intersection exists.

stem_review: Read as a student: a, b, c real; both conditions stated; 'farthest from the origin' compares the three planes; the line meets each plane once. Checked with sympy: Q = (8, 5/2, -7/2). Answer -3.50, a negative decimal as planned. Changed: removed the confusing parenthetical remark at the end of the full solution.
key_step: Parallel-and-disjoint conditions fix the planes; the distance comparison picks P3; line-plane intersection gives Q.
justification: Two chapters linked through a three-stage chain (parallel conditions, distance comparison, line-plane intersection); numerical answer. Comparable to 2025-P1-Q5 (L3) and 2026-P1-Q6 (L3).
